close_reason: Documented accepted trade-off: code already calls cleanup_orphaned_files() at startup. No code change needed.
description: Trigger: staging.rs try_stage() writes the staging file to disk before acquiring the BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. If the future is cancelled (e.g. peer disconnects) or the process is killed after fs::write succeeds but before COMMIT, the file is left on disk with no corresponding DB row. Bad behavior: orphaned staging files accumulate on disk. The code documents this and calls cleanup_orphaned_files() at startup, so the orphan is eventually cleaned up on next restart — but between crashes the disk fills if ingestion is high-volume. This is a known accepted trade-off, but should be filed for tracking.
title: staging.rs: file written before BEGIN IMMEDIATE; cancellation after write but before COMMIT leaves orphan
